signals.title: @karpathy: Dusting off this tweet from April because this gap in shared understanding of LLM capability is *widening*. It's now less "two groups of peo
signals.content: Dusting off this tweet from April because this gap in shared understanding of LLM capability is *widening*. It's now less "two groups of people speaking past each other" and more a sharp funnel. - Napkin math somewhere around 6B people (~75% of the population) have barely come in contact with LLMs at all. - Around 1-2B (~20%) are casual and infrequent users of free-tier ChatGPT-like products. This group sees derpy chatbots and treats them a bit like a better Google search, a writing aid, or etc. Maybe an agent tries to book you a flight. I have non-tech friends who (reasonably, imo) say they have not much use for it at all. Even many professionals outside of math&code are in this tier. For example, execs and many other functions spend a lot of their time talking to other people, so while they understand what is happening intellectually, it is still second-hand and a bit abstract. - Now we get to professional use of frontier-grade LLMs in math&code. Somewhere around 20M people (0.2%) see first-hand that large, complex projects that used to take them weeks/months can now be completed by agents with a prompt. Building apps, copying apps, translating apps, decompiling apps from binaries... This has all happened very quickly and recently - less than 1 year ago, I was writing code manually by hand, typing memorized computer code commands into a code editor character by character, occasionally pressing Tab to autocomplete a little chunk of code. - And finally we get to the ~5,000 people (~0.00006%) with access to frontier-grade systems internally. The external world has seen the preview. It looks like swarms of thousands of agents collaborating over weeks on software mega projects: minting zero days, running cyber attacks and defenses at machine speeds, discovering new science, advancing the frontier of mathematics. Things that would have taken top professionals in the industry years of work. Meanwhile, human review and comprehension are starting to fall behind. For example, people are still involved in the "archeology" of the OpenAI-HF incident from many months ago. Mathematicians may be poring over the 722 manuscripts on frontier mathematics for a while. The funnel is driven by a combination of factors: 1. The impact scales with ambition, problem size, and horizon. A question with a paragraph answer barely stresses the system. You need a reservoir of big, difficult problems that you really care about. This aspect drives the consumer / professional dimension of the funnel. 2. The jaggedness of the system (which I have written about a lot separately). Capability peaks in domains that are digital, verifiable and economically valuable. This is because LLM capability emerges from reinforcement learning on verifiable rewards on a curated environment mixture driven by revenue potential. This aspect primarily drives the area (e.g. math&code) dimension of the funnel. 3. Access. Free-tier, paid-tier, internal. So this is the weirdness of the moment. The general public has mostly not interacted with these systems. When they have, it looks like a derpy chatbot. The majority of professionals still see only a modest uplift. And a small sliver of professionals are experiencing the vertigo of the curve going vertical. And it is all happening at the same time.

signals.title: M4F-S/gomaa
signals.content: Gomaa — Autonomous Agent Memory OS. Persistent memory system for AI agents with Obsidian vault integration, hybrid RRF search, knowledge graphs, security gates, and MCP server.
signals.score_reason: high-value open-source ecosystem signal; agentic AI relevance. Final score: 72. Freshness: source age 0d.
signals.brief_en:
Title: M4F-S/gomaa

Gomaa is an autonomous agent memory OS that provides persistent storage for AI agents. It integrates with an Obsidian vault for user‑editable notes, uses a hybrid Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) search across vector and keyword indexes, and builds knowledge graphs to link concepts. Security gates enforce access control and data sanitisation, while the MCP server offers a unified API for retrieval, update and synchronization across agents. The system is designed for scalable, OSINT‑oriented workflows, but performance and long‑term reliability remain under evaluation.

signals.content: SociALLY is a small and extensible social media campaign AI agent harness.
signals.score_reason: high-value open-source ecosystem signal; agentic AI relevance. Final score: 58. Freshness: source age 0d.
signals.brief_en:
Title: 315Concepts/sally-agent-pipeline

Brief: SociALLY is a lightweight, extensible AI agent designed to automate social‑media campaign tasks. It can ingest public data, generate content drafts, schedule posts, and perform basic sentiment monitoring. The system is modular, allowing integration of additional analytics or platform APIs. Current capabilities are limited to major platforms (Twitter, Facebook, Instagram) and rely on publicly available OSINT sources; performance on niche networks or private groups is unverified. Deployment requires minimal infrastructure, but ongoing maintenance and data‑privacy compliance are the operator’s responsibility.

الملخص: SociALLY هو وكيل ذكاء اصطناعي خفيف الوزن وقابل للتوسيع يُستخدم لأتمتة مهام الحملات على وسائل التواصل الاجتماعي. يستطيع جمع البيانات العامة، توليد مسودات المحتوى، جدولة النشر، ومراقبة المشاعر الأساسية. النظام معيّن بنية معيارية تسمح بدمج تحليلات إضافية أو واجهات برمجة تطبيقات المنصات. القدرات الحالية تقتصر على المنصات الرئيسية (تويتر، فيسبوك، إنستغرام) وتعتمد على مصادر OSINT العامة؛ ولا يُعرف مدى فعاليته على الشبكات المتخصصة أو المجموعات الخاصة. يتطلب النشر بنية تحتية بسيطة، لكن الصيانة المستمرة والامتثال لخصوصية البيانات تقع على عاتق المشغل.

signals.content: Mac-hosted multi-agent coding fleet: board at mac.jays.services, Slack #agent-sync, Shellular.
signals.score_reason: high-value open-source ecosystem signal; agentic AI relevance. Final score: 58. Freshness: source age 0d.
signals.brief_en:
Title: Simple-With-Us/AI-Fleet-Coordinator

A macOS‑hosted multi‑agent coding fleet is coordinated via a web board (mac.jays.services), a Slack channel (#agent‑sync), and a Shellular interface. The system enables distributed code generation, testing, and deployment across macOS nodes. Current capabilities include parallel script execution, version‑controlled repository sync, and basic health monitoring. Limitations: performance depends on macOS hardware availability; security posture is still under assessment; integration with non‑mac environments is not yet supported.
